stem: The authorized work order called for selective canopy adjustment, but the completion record only says “defoliated.” What is missing for performance review?
choices: The completion record needs planned-versus-actual scope, intensity and location of work, timing, and post-work observations so performance can be linked to what was actually done.
The word “defoliated” is sufficient if the same team normally uses a standard intensity and technique.
Only the worker identity is needed because the authorized work order already defines the intended scope.
A later room-average yield can substitute for detailed completion records if the crop performs within target.
rationale: A performance review needs to know not just that work occurred, but what was actually done compared with the plan. Scope, intensity, location, timing, and post-work observations are necessary to relate outcomes to the intervention. A technique label or worker name alone cannot establish whether execution matched the authorized work order or explain spatial differences in recovery.
